First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨{e}^{2t}+5,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨{e}^{2t}+5,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨\int ({e}^{2t}+5)\,\text{d}t,\,\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{e}^{2t}}{2}+5t+{c}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)+{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{e}^{2t}}{2}+5t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)⟩+⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{e}^{2t}}{2}+5t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)⟩+C,\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $C$ is an arbitrary (vector) constant of integration.
